AI × Web3 Daily · 2026-07-28

AI & Web3 Industry Daily

Today’s main thread is AI compute capital formation, safety and regulatory implementation, RWA, and on-chain market infrastructure. This report selects 10 verified stories; every chart uses explicit figures from the included news items.

10Top stories included
13Referenced sources
5Items with quantified funding or market data
3Industry segments covered

Trend Commentary

The largest variable on the AI side remains compute and capital: NVIDIA, OpenAI, Meta, and Orange all point to a shift from model-only competition toward data-center and GPU-supply competition. Regulation and safety are also intensifying, with the EU, the US, and China advancing more concrete AI risk-governance frameworks. On the Web3 side, market attention continues to center on tokenized assets, institutional on-chain trading infrastructure, and Ethereum L1 scaling.

Top Stories

#01AI compute financing

NVIDIA and Safe Superintelligence Form Long-Term Strategic Partnership

NVIDIA confirmed an investment in Ilya Sutskever’s SSI and access to its Vera Rubin platform, saying the partnership will help SSI increase compute capacity by an order of magnitude; media reports citing people familiar with the matter put the investment commitment at about $5 billion.[1][2]

Key figures: official statement says compute capacity increases 10x; the dollar figure is media-reported, not officially disclosed.

#02AI data centers

NVIDIA Reportedly Negotiates Financing Guarantee for OpenAI’s 10GW Ohio Data Center

Bloomberg reported that the guarantee could reach about $250 billion and that the project is planned to go online in 2028, but talks remain early and could fail or change.[3]

Key figures: 10GW data center; financing guarantee of up to about $250 billion.

#03AI infrastructure

BlackRock Completes $12.5 Billion Debt Financing for Meta’s Texas AI Data Center

The reported project targets up to 1GW of AI compute capacity. BlackRock affiliates hold 80%, Meta holds 20%, and the debt is supported by Meta lease commitments.[4]

Key figures: $12.5 billion in bonds; demand reportedly reached about $20 billion.

#04European AI cloud

Orange and Morrison Plan 50:50 French Data-Center Joint Venture

Reuters reported that the two parties plan a data-center platform for AI and cloud demand, targeting 400MW of capacity with planned investment of €3 billion, or about $3.41 billion.[5]

Key figures: 400MW target capacity; about €3 billion planned investment.

#05AI safety

OpenAI Releases GPT-Red to Improve Prompt-Injection Robustness with Automated Red Teaming

OpenAI said GPT-Red reached an 84% attack success rate in an indirect prompt-injection arena, compared with 13% for human red teams, and was used to train GPT-5.6 safety.[6]

Key figures: GPT-Red 84% vs. human red teams 13%; vendor-reported, so independent replication remains important.

#06AI regulation

EU AI Act Enters Key 2026 Implementation Period Alongside AI-Cybersecurity Action Plan

EU materials list transparency rules taking effect in August 2026, while high-risk system obligations extend into December 2027 and August 2028. The action plan emphasizes safe use of advanced AI, stronger cyber resilience, and broader European AI cybersecurity capacity.[7][8]

Key figures: three action-plan objectives; multiple AI Act obligations phase in over time.

#07China AI governance

China’s Anthropomorphic AI Interaction Rules Take Effect as WAIC Statement Emphasizes Global AI Governance

The Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services took effect on July 15, 2026, covering AI companions and services for children and elderly users. The WAIC Chair Statement highlighted classification, risk alerts, and agent boundary-setting.[9][10]

Key figures: issued by five departments; effective date July 15, 2026.

#08Multimodal safety

FlowGuard Paper Proposes Internal Consistency Checks for Multimodal Attacks

The arXiv paper says FlowGuard monitors cross-modal internal consistency, reducing attack success rates from above 90% to below 15% with less than 3% utility loss.[11]

Key figures: attack success rate from >90% to <15%; preprint results still require replication.

#09Web3 funding

Alpaca Raises $135 Million to Scale Tokenized Markets and AI-Native Brokerage Infrastructure

Alpaca announced a $135 million equity financing round and $435 million in total new financing to scale API-first, agent-first brokerage infrastructure and tokenized markets.[12]

Key figures: $135 million equity round; $435 million total new financing.

#10Web3 market

BTC and ETH Edge Higher as Derivatives Volume Expands

TokenPost’s market briefing showed BTC at $64,898.47, up 0.40% over 24 hours, and ETH at $1,947.74, up 1.83%, while 24-hour derivatives volume rose 118.42%.[13]

Key figures: BTC +0.40%; ETH +1.83%; derivatives volume +118.42%.
